questions.question: What is the primary goal of the distributed consensus algorithm described?

answers.a: To ensure every process runs indefinitely
answers.b: To synchronize clocks across distributed systems
answers.c: To agree on a single value among all non-faulty processes

explanations.a: Incorrect: The algorithm is designed to terminate after consensus is reached.
explanations.b: Incorrect: Synchronizing clocks is not the purpose of this algorithm.
explanations.c: Correct: The algorithm ensures all non-faulty processes agree on a single value.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Encryption is not the focus of this consensus algorithm.

questions.question: How many rounds does the consensus algorithm run to tolerate up to f process failures?

explanations.a: Incorrect: The algorithm runs one more round than the number of failures.
explanations.b: Correct: The algorithm runs for f+1 rounds to tolerate up to f failures.
explanations.c: Incorrect: This overestimates the required number of rounds.
explanations.d: Incorrect: This is not required for the fail-stop model.

questions.question: What is the fail-stop model in distributed systems?

answers.a: A model where processes fail and then restart automatically
answers.b: A model where processes may crash and stop permanently
answers.c: A model where processes never fail
answers.d: A model where processes send incorrect messages intentionally

explanations.a: Incorrect: Processes do not restart in the fail-stop model.
explanations.b: Correct: In the fail-stop model, processes may crash and stop permanently.
explanations.c: Incorrect: The model specifically accounts for process failures.
explanations.d: Incorrect: This describes Byzantine failures, not fail-stop failures.

questions.question: What happens in a round if a process does not broadcast its current value?

answers.b: The process broadcasts a default value
answers.c: No value is received from that process in the round

explanations.a: Incorrect: Faulty processes are defined by failure to operate, including failure to broadcast in a round.
explanations.b: Incorrect: There is no default value broadcast in this algorithm.
explanations.c: Correct: If a process does not broadcast, no value is received from it.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Processes do not restart in this algorithm.

questions.question: What ensures that the consensus value does not change once it is reached?

answers.c: Processes are non-Byzantine and do not alter the agreed value
answers.d: Consensus is achieved before any processes fail

explanations.a: Incorrect: Processes do not restart in this algorithm.
explanations.b: Incorrect: Values can be broadcast multiple times during the algorithm.
explanations.c: Correct: Non-Byzantine processes ensure the agreed value is not altered.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Consensus is designed to tolerate failures, not avoid them entirely.

questions.question: Why is the fail-stop model suitable for this consensus algorithm?

answers.a: It assumes all processes will eventually fail
answers.b: It avoids dealing with adversarial (Byzantine) processes
answers.c: It guarantees synchronization of all processes
answers.d: It requires processes to restart on failure

explanations.a: Incorrect: The fail-stop model assumes some processes may fail but not all.
explanations.b: Correct: The fail-stop model simplifies the algorithm by avoiding Byzantine behavior.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Synchronization is not guaranteed for all processes, only agreement among non-faulty ones.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Processes do not restart in the fail-stop model.

questions.question: In the consensus algorithm, what mathematical operation ensures agreement among processes?

answers.a: Taking the maximum of all received values
answers.b: Taking the minimum of all received values including own value
answers.c: Taking the average of all received values
answers.d: Taking the sum of all received values

explanations.a: Incorrect: The algorithm uses minimum, not maximum.
explanations.b: Correct: Each process updates x to min(x, all received values).
explanations.c: Incorrect: Average is not used in this consensus algorithm.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Sum is not used in this consensus algorithm.

questions.question: What is the key insight behind why the algorithm guarantees agreement in f+1 rounds?

answers.a: All processes will have failed by round f+1
answers.b: At least one round exists where all non-faulty processes can broadcast
answers.c: The minimum value is always known from the first round
answers.d: Byzantine processes are eliminated after f rounds

explanations.a: Incorrect: The algorithm assumes some processes remain non-faulty.
explanations.b: Correct: There exists at least one round where all good processes can broadcast their values.
explanations.c: Incorrect: The minimum value may not be known initially due to failures.
explanations.d: Incorrect: The algorithm assumes non-Byzantine processes throughout.

questions.question: What condition must be satisfied for the consensus algorithm to guarantee termination and correctness?

answers.a: All processes must start with the same initial value
answers.b: No more than f processes can fail, where f < n
answers.c: Processes must communicate in a specific order
answers.d: The network must be completely connected at all times

explanations.a: Incorrect: Processes can start with different initial values.
explanations.b: Correct: The algorithm tolerates up to f failures where f < n.
explanations.c: Incorrect: There is no specific communication order required.
explanations.d: Incorrect: The algorithm can handle network partitions as long as failure assumptions hold.
